This is impacting our clinical workflows and the CEO is asking for an urgent update. Can we get an immediate triage and a mitigation plan (minutes -> hours)?

Requesting an executive-level call if needed; we want to avoid a prolonged outage.

Thanks,

Quick technical summary from initial triage (logs + pcap review):
- We see bursts where the transit-proxy (their IPs) is returning RSTs while simultaneously opening new connections. Pattern is consistent with NAT translation table pressure on the proxy (many ephemeral ports, lots of retries).
- DNS: there are rapid DNS A-query bursts from their proxy cluster for our edge hostname around the same time window; TTL is low on their side which amplifies churn.
- Our edge LB shows no CPU/GPU saturation; token-generating services are healthy. Most of the timeouts are failing during the TCP handshake/shortly after connect.

Immediate recommended mitigations (minutes-hours):
1) Ask Parkside to temporarily bypass the transit-proxy for Redwood hostnames and route via their VPC peering to our peered subnet (fastest path).
2) Increase proxy ephemeral port pool and MAX_CONN settings on Parkside side (we can provide recommended configs).
3) Activate short-lived connection rate-limiting and retry-backoff at our edge to reduce amplification.
4) Prepare controlled failover: flip traffic to the dedicated peering path during a 1-hour maintenance window.

We need quick sign-off from Parkside to proceed with (1) or (4). If they can't change the proxy config immediately, we can do a temporary traffic shaping rule on our edge to reduce tail risk while we schedule the maintenance.

I'll attach a diff of suggested proxy config changes and an annotated pcap snippet.

Jonas
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Aaron / team — thanks for the quick report and the pcap. We diagnosed the likely root cause: intermittent NAT/translation pressure and connection churn on the transit-proxy path (combined with their low DNS TTL) is driving connection failures and long handshakes that manifest as long tail latency and 504s.

Proposed immediate plan (we can execute tonight with your sign-off):
- Option A (fastest): temporarily route Parkside's traffic for *.api.redwood.example.com to the VPC peering path (bypass transit-proxy). This requires a single CIDR route add on your side and no infra changes on ours. Estimated time to flip: 20-40 minutes.
- Option B (config): apply proxy ephemeral-port and connection limits changes (we provided a config diff). Estimated time: 1-3 hours, depends on your ops schedule.
- Fallback: we will apply edge-level smoothing to reduce retries causing amplification while we coordinate.

We propose a controlled maintenance window to do Option A: 2027-04-03 02:00-03:00 PT. We'll perform the failover, monitor metrics (latency, 5xx), and rollback if we see any regression. We will also post a follow-up RCA and provide a copy of the proxy config diff we suggest.

Please reply with your preferred option and confirm the maintenance window. If you prefer us to pursue Option B instead, let us know and we'll standby to coordinate.

Best,
Grace
